terms.grammar: verb, irregular (inter + sum), with the dative
terms.gloss: take part in, be present at
evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.6.1: omnibus negōtiīs nōn interfuit sōlum, sed praefuit
terms.comment: With the dative of what one takes part in, or in and the ablative.

terms.grammar: adjective particeps, participis, with esse and the genitive
terms.gloss: have a part in, share in
evidence: Cic. Att. 9.10.5: hujus igitur bellī ego particeps et socius et adjūtor esse cōgor

terms.gloss: draw in, involve; (with sē) get mixed up in
terms.comment: Of drawing someone into an affair, or meddling in it.

evidence: Cic. Off. 2.40: contrahendīs negōtiīs implicārī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Mostly passive: to be caught up in business, a war, mistakes.

terms.gloss: be engaged in, be busy with, be active in
evidence: Cic. Phil. 12.25: quī in rē pūblicā versantur (Lewis & Short s.v. reprehēnsiō)
terms.comment: Literally “to turn about in” a thing: in rē pūblicā versārī, to be active in public life.

phrases.latin: quī nōn sōlum interfuit iīs rēbus, sed etiam praefuit
phrases.english: who was not only involved in these matters but in charge of them

phrases.latin: Ita tū istaec tua miscētō nē mē admisceās.
phrases.english: Stir up those affairs of yours, then, without involving me.

phrases.latin: Nē tē admisce: nēmō accūsat, Syre, tē
phrases.english: Keep out of it: nobody is accusing you, Syrus

sources: Lewis & Short: intersum · Lewis & Short: particeps · Lewis & Short: admisceo · Lewis & Short: implico
